Usage

ISS (Intrinsic Shape Signatures, equivalent to a 3D Harris) keypoint detector. Uses the smallest eigenvalue λ3 of the local covariance as the saliency, restricts candidates to points whose eigenvalues are distinct (i.e. well-defined orientation), and sparsely selects them via NMS. Rotation-invariant. Returns an array of point indices.

Arguments:

• points (N,3). radius: radius of the neighbourhood sphere for saliency (same units as the point cloud).

• nms_radius: non-maximum suppression distance. If None, 0.6*radius.

• gamma21 / gamma32: upper limits of the eigenvalue ratios λ2/λ1, λ3/λ2 (default 0.99). Only points where both are

below these are candidates (excluding points whose ratio is close to 1 = isotropic, with undetermined orientation).

• max_kp: maximum number returned. min_neighbors: points with fewer neighbours than this are not candidates (default 8).

Procedure: at each point gather the neighbours within radius, form the 2nd-order moment matrix with the point of interest as origin, (qᵀq)/n, and obtain its eigenvalues λ1≥λ2≥λ3 (excluded if λ1 is 1e-12 or less). Using λ3 as saliency, scan in descending order; greedy NMS discards those closer than nms_radius to an already accepted point. Returns an int64 array of point indices (in descending saliency). Length 0 if there are no candidates.

Note: the neighbourhood is centred on the point of interest (not the centroid), so even for points on a plane λ3 is not exactly 0. It is a Python loop doing a neighbour search at every point, so for clouds above tens of thousands of points thin them out with voxel_grid_downsample first. It feeds directly into the keypoint input of shot_descriptor, and register_shot calls it internally with 0.6× radius and NMS 0.3×.

The 3d op iss_keypoints bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps gamma21 (default 0.99), b sweeps gamma32 (default 0.99).
